commonCauses: Cracked EGR cooler with internal coolant leak
Cooler flow restricted by carbon/soot buildup
Broken return spring inside the cooler
notes: Well-documented on this exact engine/chassis combination. Often shows up with no other symptom besides the check-engine light, or alongside unexplained coolant loss and faint sweet-smelling white exhaust smoke — inspect the EGR cooler itself, not just the EGR valve, before assuming a head gasket problem.

commonCauses: Fractured swirl flap shaft or linkage
Actuator motor binding against carbon buildup
notes: BMW-specific hex fault code (format shown as reported via ISTA/dealer-level tools — a generic OBD-II reader may present it differently). If flaps have physically fractured, inspect for ingested debris before returning the engine to service — this is the failure mode that can cause catastrophic cylinder damage.

description: Swirl Flap Position Sensor — Signal Too Low / Implausible
commonCauses: Worn or seized flap linkage reported as a false 'broken' signal
Carbon buildup preventing full flap travel
notes: BMW-specific hex fault code. Often triggers limp mode even when the flaps themselves are only gummed up with carbon rather than actually broken — worth a manual inspection before assuming the worst.

description: Transfer Case ECU — Clutch Failure, Stuck Open (Rear-Wheel-Drive Only Mode)
commonCauses: Degraded or neglected transfer case fluid
Skipped adaptation reset after a fluid service
notes: BMW-specific hex fault code reported via dealer-level diagnostics; exact code presentation can vary by tool/software version — confirm against ISTA for this VIN. Often paired with a 4x4/drivetrain warning light and a grinding or binding feel in slow, tight turns.
